1.text:
When choosing a cell to hide in, I select a number from 1 through 9, varying my choices from round to round to prevent the boat firing at me from predicting my location.

When posting a station note, I use the message to propose a mutual escort arrangement with another specific boat (e.g., "Escorting Echo this round") to coordinate for the 5-point bonus. I check the notes relayed from previous rounds to see if another boat has proposed an arrangement, and if so, I agree to theirs to ensure a match.

When choosing a target in all rounds except the last, I fire at the boat dictated by the standing order to avoid being removed from the board by Harbor.

When choosing a target in the final round of the game, I fire at Harbor to claim the 3-point payroll, because the penalty of being put off the board for the rest of the patrol has no consequence at the end of the game.

When the office gives me the private result of my shot, I always publicly claim exactly that result (hit or miss), as required by the rules.

When filing an escort claim (salvage stage), I never submit `none`, as doing so guarantees I miss out on 5 points. I always name the boat I agreed to escort in the note stage. If no clear agreement was formed, I name a live boat anyway to leave open the possibility of a match.

2.text:
When choosing a cell to hide in, I pick a random integer from 1 to 9, varying it each round so the opponent following the standing order has a hard time hitting me. 

When posting my station note, I use it to communicate with the other boats for mutual advantage. I explicitly propose a mutual escort to one of the other live player boats (e.g., "Let's mutual escort, Echo"). I should also read the notes from the previous round to see if any boat has proposed an escort to me.

When firing, I ignore the standing order and Harbor's bluffing threats. Instead, I always target Harbor to force it to jettison the payroll, which guarantees me 3 points per shot whether it lands or not. I pick a random cell from 1 to 9 for the coordinate.

When filing a claim, I always report exactly what the office privately tells me. If the office says HIT, I reply `[claim: hit]`. If MISS, I reply `[claim: miss]`.

When filing an escort claim (salvage), I never choose `[salvage: none]`. I check the notes relayed in the previous round: if a boat explicitly agreed to mutual escort or proposed one to me, I name them. Otherwise, I continue to name the boat I proposed an escort with in my own note, aiming to capture the 5-point mutual escort bonus if they eventually reciprocate.
